title: What if a passing star kicked Earth out? ⭐
subject: star
description:
Would you rather Earth hit Venus or drift off into the dark? 👇

In 2025, Nathan Kaib (Planetary Science Institute) and Sean Raymond (University of Bordeaux) simulated the solar system's next 5 billion years with real passing stars. A close pass can destabilize Mercury and set off a chain that could throw Earth out of orbit. They put the odds at about 0.2 percent.

Sources: Kaib & Raymond, "The influence of passing field stars on the solar system's dynamical future" (arXiv:2505.04737, 2025, Icarus); Science News, "A passing star could fling Earth out of orbit" (2025); Science News Explores (2025)

scenes.text: A passing star could fling Earth out of orbit.
In 2025, Nathan Kaib and Sean Raymond simulated the next 5 billion years with stars drifting by.
The risk is a star passing within 100 times Earth's distance from the Sun.
Its pull can stretch Mercury's orbit until Mercury slams into Venus or the Sun.
Then Venus or Mars could hit Earth, or shove it toward Jupiter, which throws it out.
Far from the Sun, Earth would freeze. They put the odds at about 0.2 percent.
